related_questions.question: What are the 7 most common lung diseases?

text_blocks.snippet: The 7 most common lung diseases are: Asthma, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Lung Cancer, Pneumonia, Bronchitis, Pulmonary Edema, and Pulmonary Embolism. These conditions affect the airways, lung tissue, or blood vessels, impacting the body's ability to breathe effectively.
snippet_highlighted_words: Asthma, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Lung Cancer, Pneumonia, Bronchitis, Pulmonary Edema, and Pulmonary Embolism

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at each:

list.title: Asthma:
list.snippet: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways, causing them to narrow and swell, leading to wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath.

list.title: COPD:
list.snippet: A group of lung diseases (including emphysema and chronic bronchitis) that cause airflow blockage and breathing problems.

list.title: Lung Cancer:
list.snippet: Cancer that begins in the lungs, often linked to smoking, but can also affect non-smokers.

list.title: Pneumonia:
list.snippet: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus.

list.title: Bronchitis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, the airways that carry air to your lungs. Can be acute (short-term) or chronic (long-term).

list.title: Pulmonary Edema:
list.snippet: A condition in which excess fluid builds up in the lungs, making it difficult to breathe.

list.title: Pulmonary Embolism:
list.snippet: A blockage in one of the pulmonary arteries in your lungs, often caused by blood clots that travel from other parts of the body.

text_blocks.snippet: Lung diseases encompass a wide range of conditions that affect the respiratory system, primarily impacting breathing and lung function. These diseases can be broadly categorized into obstructive, restrictive, and infectious lung diseases, among others. Some common examples include asthma, COPD (including emphysema and chronic bronchitis), lung cancer, pneumonia, and pulmonary fibrosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: asthma, COPD (including emphysema and chronic bronchitis), lung cancer, pneumonia, and pulmonary fibrosis

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at some common types:
1. Obstructive Lung Diseases: These conditions impair airflow, making it difficult to exhale.

list.title: Asthma:
list.snippet: Characterized by airway inflammation and bronchospasms, leading to wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing.

list.title: COPD:
list.snippet: A progressive disease including emphysema and chronic bronchitis, causing persistent airflow limitation and breathing difficulties.

list.title: Emphysema:
list.snippet: Damage to the air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs, leading to shortness of breath and difficulty exhaling.

list.title: Bronchitis (acute and chronic):
list.snippet: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, causing coughing and mucus production.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. Restrictive Lung Diseases: These conditions reduce lung volume and the ability to fully expand the lungs.

list.snippet: Pulmonary Fibrosis: Scarring of lung tissue, making it stiff and difficult to expand.
Sarcoidosis: Inflammation that can affect multiple organs, including the lungs, leading to scarring and breathing problems.
Pneumothorax: Air leakage into the space between the lung and chest wall, causing lung collapse.

text_blocks.snippet: 3. Infectious Lung Diseases: These are caused by various pathogens like bacteria, viruses, or fungi.

list.snippet: Pneumonia: Infection of the lungs, causing inflammation and fluid buildup.
Tuberculosis: A bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs, but can spread to other organs.
Lung Cancer: Abnormal cell growth in the lungs, often linked to smoking and other factors.
Pulmonary Edema: Fluid buildup in the lungs, often due to heart problems.
Pleural Effusion: Fluid buildup in the space between the lung and chest wall.
Mesothelioma: Cancer caused by asbestos exposure, affecting the lining of the lungs.

text_blocks.snippet: This is not an exhaustive list, and many other lung conditions exist, including rare diseases and those affecting specific populations.
